# Riverbend Health System — Company Context

- **What it is:** a nonprofit **integrated health system** serving the (fictional) Riverbend
  metro and surrounding rural counties. Four acute-care hospitals, an employed medical group
  (~640 providers), 22 outpatient/ambulatory clinics, and home-health and hospice services.
- **Scale:** ~1,180 licensed beds; ~9,400 employees; ~$2.1B net patient revenue; ~118,000
  annual ED visits system-wide; a Level II trauma center at the flagship.
- **The four hospitals:**
  - **Riverbend General Hospital** — flagship, downtown; **512 licensed beds**; Level II
    trauma, tertiary referral center, the main OR and cath-lab site.
  - **Riverbend West Medical Center** — suburban; 380 licensed beds; includes the system's
    inpatient behavioral health unit.
  - **Lakeside Community Hospital** — 188 licensed beds; community/secondary care.
  - **Cascade Rural Hospital** — 100 licensed beds; critical-access-style rural facility.
- **Payer mix:** roughly Medicare 44%, Medicaid 21%, Commercial 30%, self-pay/other 5% — a
  Medicare-heavy book that makes CMS quality penalties and payer rates material to margin.
- **Governance:** governed by a community board chaired by
  [Eleanor Whitfield](../people/eleanor-whitfield.md); led by CEO
  [Marcus Bell](../people/marcus-bell.md).
- **Strategic context (2026):** thin operating margin (~1.8%) under wage inflation and agency
  labor cost; a system-wide **Epic** EHR rollout in progress; a **New Patient Tower** under
  construction at the flagship; and a confidential restructuring,
  [Lantern](../projects/lantern.md).
- **Regulatory frame:** accredited by **The Joint Commission** (deemed status for CMS);
  participates in CMS value-based programs. See [operations](operations.md).
